IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for service=kv-router env=prod — spike in 95th/99th latency and a large increase in memtable entries. Alert: KV_CACHE_GROWTH > 500k in 10m. thread:1777777777
Maya Lin: acked. seeing huge outgoing traffic to redis + models spiking token generation counts. attaching quick metrics snapshot in a sec.
Owen Patel: on it. first glance: continuous-batcher avg batch_size jumped from 6 -> 60 in the last 8m, and prefix-key count exploded. could be a key churn/invalidation loop.
Jamie R.: any customer-facing impact? CS Lead is on standby.
CS Lead: we already have 2 customers reporting degraded latency on inference endpoints (~2-6s tail) — flagged via support. putting them on notify list.
Maya Lin: log tail (sample):
```
[2026-04-12T02:12:43Z] kv-router: put key="/pref/templ/abcd1234" size=512
[2026-04-12T02:12:44Z] kv-router: put key="/pref/templ/efgh5678" size=520
[2026-04-12T02:12:44Z] batcher: batch_size=48 route=shortseq
[2026-04-12T02:12:45Z] tokenizer: fingerprint=0x9a1b2c expected=0x3f7d8e
```
Maya Lin: note the tokenizer fingerprint mismatch. looks like tokenization version drift caused new prefix keys to be generated (old keys didn't match), causing cache blowup.
SRE Oncall: confirmed. If tokenizer changed in canary earlier and rehashed prefix keys, cache misses would generate many new entries. Continuous batching then exacerbates by creating many small unique keys in each batch.
Owen Patel: immediate mitigations I'm testing: 1) throttle batcher max_size -> 12, 2) set eviction aggressive TTL for newly created prefix keys, 3) enable prefix-collation fallback to original hash algorithm. Applying 1 & 2 now.
SRE Oncall: plz run the command to update runtime flags.
Owen Patel: running:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/kv-router BATCH_MAX_SIZE=12 KV_NEWKEY_TTL=60
# rolling restart on small cohort
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/kv-router --selector=pool=prod-canary
```
Owen Patel: done. reducing batch max size; watch metric: batch_size_p50 fell to 8 within 40s, new-key rate down ~75%.
Maya Lin: memory pressure trending down, 95th latency improving from 1.9s -> 420ms. still seeing old hot keys in redis but eviction is catching up.
CS Lead: pinging affected customers: "We've identified a transient cache key churn causing higher latency; mitigation in progress. ETA 30m."
Jamie R.: do we need a rollback of the tokenizer canary?
SRE Oncall: let's freeze the tokenizer canary and mark it for rollback if the rehashing persists. Owen, can you snapshot which canary hosts received tokenizer update?
Owen Patel: listing canary pods now, 3/6 had v2-tokenizer. marking them to pin v1.
Maya Lin: creating a short-lived hotfix: keep v2 but add compatibility mode to accept old fingerprints (rehash fallback). patch PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv-router/pull/4129 (WIP).
SRE Oncall: for now keep throttles and TTLs in place. escalate if new-key-rate > 10k/min again.
IncidentBot: paging policy: SLO impact tracked. Severity set to SEV2. Incident channel created.
Maya Lin: handoff to Night SRE in 30m window — leaving notes and runbook: 
- cause: tokenizer fingerprint mismatch after canary deploy -> rehashed prefix keys -> cache churn -> continuous-batcher amplifies key cardinality
- immediate mitigations applied: batch max=12, KV_NEWKEY_TTL=60, canary freeze
- next steps: complete compatibility fallback PR, gradually revert canary or roll forward with compatibility, run cache compaction job overnight
- customer comms: CS to send updated ETA 30m -> 2h depending on compaction
Owen Patel: adding a quick script to scan for high-cardinality prefixes and tag them for TTL eviction:
```
python tools/scan_prefixes.py --threshold 1000 --mark-ttl 60 --dry-run
```
SRE Oncall: good. leaving this in the channel for handoff. I'm taking long-term ownership for patch rollout. ping me if any spike.
CS Lead: thanks. I'll update the customer thread and keep support tickets open.
Jamie R.: filing incident ticket for postmortem: include deploy timeline, tokenizer release notes, and batching config delta. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.
Maya Lin: final note before handoff: watch for template-driven prompts — templating drift was observed where template variable order caused different prefix strings even with same underlying prompt. add template normalization to postmortem.
SRE Oncall: ack. handing off to Night SRE. leaving channel open for any urgent follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
